Instrument Junction Box Specification Checklist

An instrument junction box is specified on a datasheet before it is ordered, and missing one line on that sheet is a common cause of rework at site. The checklist below collects the requirements covered in this article into one table that can be used when preparing or reviewing a JB datasheet.

ItemTypical requirement
Signal groupingSeparate boxes for analog, digital, power and fieldbus
IS segregationDedicated IS box, or approved separation from non IS wiring
Hazardous areaEx e, Ex d or Ex i to suit zone, gas group and T class
Ingress protectionIP56 minimum outdoors, higher for washdown
MaterialSS316L for coastal and offshore, GRP for chemical areas
TerminalsRated for conductor size, usually 1.5 or 2.5 square mm
SparesAbout 10 to 20 percent spare terminals and multicore pairs
Cable entriesBottom entry, certified glands, stopping plugs on unused holes
EarthingExternal earth stud plus isolated instrument shield bar
LabellingBox tag, terminal and core numbers matching the JB schedule

Quick review steps

  1. Count every instrument and its terminals per loop from the instrument list.
  2. Add shield terminals and the spare allowance, then pick the multicore size.
  3. Check the area classification and choose the protection concept.
  4. Confirm IP rating, material and gland certification match each other.
  5. Check that shields are earthed at one end only, usually the control room.

Once these items are fixed, the box size and terminal layout follow directly.
